# How to keep a product identical in AI video — no warped logos or labels

**Product photos become a lock sheet and 2–4 angle reference pack, so Seedance or Kling shots keep shape, color and label.**

<p><img src="https://s3.varg.ai/files/194b94d0-58ff-4e8b-91de-4f1959d04013/file_5bd801ceb44e.webp" alt="Side-by-side car-seat product shots: on the left the product drifts in shape, on the right the lock-pack version keeps it identical as hands fit it." width="480"></p>

Turns product photos into AI video shots that keep the product identical: a lock sheet (fixed geometry, fixed surface, allowed motion), a reference pack of 2-4 angles passed as @image roles to Seedance 2.5 or Kling 4, a camera-risk ladder (locked frame → push-in → slide → small orbit), banned motion words, one action per 4-6 s shot, a drift check with varg video_analyze, and the real packshot composited back where text must be exact. Fixes the #1 "looks fake" tell in AI product ads: warped logos, melted labels, products that change shape or size between shots. Use when a product drifts, morphs, changes color or loses its label in AI video, when someone asks for "consistent product", "keep my logo", "product looks different in every shot", or before a batch of product videos for TikTok Shop, Meta or Amazon. Not for people and characters staying the same (use varg-consistent-characters or varg-character-design).

```bash
npx skills add vargHQ/skills --skill varg-product-lock                # Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok, Gemini CLI, OpenCode…
gh skill install vargHQ/skills varg-product-lock --agent github-copilot --scope user
# or all 82 skills as a Claude Code plugin:
claude plugin marketplace add vargHQ/skills
claude plugin install varg@varg
```

## Ask your agent

- "My bottle's label melts in every AI shot — lock it from ./front.jpg and ./side.jpg before I make 10 clips"
- "Make 4 product shots of our car seat gap filler where it keeps its exact wedge shape"
- "Check these 3 generated clips against my product photos and tell me which ones drifted"
